purpose: Issue #53 evidence set and the market theses it supports. Every OBSERVED record here was read out of a file in this repository and cites the exact key it was read from. No record was obtained from an external provider: acquisition/signal-intelligence/providers.json shows which providers are CONTRACT_ONLY, and a CONTRACT_ONLY provider is refused as a source of OBSERVED evidence by lib/normalize.mjs.
evidence_note: Nothing in this file was scraped, inferred from a trend, or written to make a thesis look better corroborated than it is. Two of the three theses below deliberately fail the 2-Signal Rule, and that is the correct current answer.

signals.observation_summary: PostHog-recorded owned funnel behaviour for the 30 days to 2026-08-27: 56 funnel_view, 15 primary_cta_click, 17 checkout_click. Commercial intent exists on the owned funnel. These counts are site-wide rather than attributed to any one thesis, verified_social_utm_pageviews_last_30d is 0, and revenue-os/metrics.json records stripe_live_payment_intents 0, so no purchase has occurred.
signals.rights_policy_notes: The operator's own analytics. No third-party rights and no scraping involved.

signals.topic: SaaS and AI subscription waste benchmarks
signals.observation_summary: A recorded public-search pass on 2026-08-27 found SaaS and AI subscription waste widely reported at 25-30% of spend, with AI subscription proliferation described as three AI assistants doing the same job. The pass names Zylo SaaS spend management material, RedHub AI SaaS cost and audit posts, and a G2 2026 SaaS spend management roundup.
signals.rights_policy_notes: Public search results summarised by the operator into revenue-os/metrics.json. No content was copied and no login-required or scraped source was used; the recorded pass states public search only.

signals.topic: Shadow AI spend and CFO budget accountability
signals.observation_summary: The same recorded pass found shadow AI spend and CFO budget accountability described as a distinct 2026 term: enterprise AI spend up 108% year on year, 78% of CFO and IT leaders reporting unbudgeted AI charges, organisations moving to quarterly AI and SaaS spend audits, and some capping per-tool or per-employee AI spend.
signals.rights_policy_notes: Public search results summarised by the operator. No content copied.

signals.topic: AI workflow automation ROI content saturation
signals.observation_summary: The same pass recorded that general SMB AI-workflow-automation ROI content is common and non-differentiated in aggregate dev community posts, with no distinct new angle found. This is demand that already exists and is already served, so it lowers the differentiation score rather than raising confidence.
signals.rights_policy_notes: Aggregate observation recorded by the operator. No individual post is reproduced.

signals.topic: Agent payback period once human review is counted
signals.observation_summary: The acquisition demand signal for this thesis cites only that a live calculator page was built for the intent and that it carries a payment link. That is an asset fact, not a demand observation, so this record is filed as an assumption about buyer behaviour rather than as evidence of it.

Three Return Gate pageviews were recorded in the seven days to 2026-08-27, and the measurement note states the pageviews in that window were reported as direct referrer traffic. This is a measured number and it is very small; it is not evidence of external demand.

signals.topic: Recurring checking behaviour as a site asset
signals.observation_summary: A COMPLETE owner-approved source package argues that recurring checking behaviour, rather than article volume, is what makes a site durable, and works through public examples of services built on that behaviour. It is owner-authored material and shares the owned independence group with the operator's own analytics.
signals.rights_policy_notes: Owner-authored. content/note-publish-queue/README.md defines the COMPLETE criteria this package meets.
